name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz largely shut; mine claims 4 Nov
summary: Hormuz largely shut; Iran's IRGC claims four tankers hit mines on 4 Nov
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on 4 Nov that four tankers hit mines and caught fire south of Hormuz and that it detained two vessels; the claims have not been independently verified (bne IntelliNews; IranWire). UKMTO reported a tanker's engine room hit by two projectiles off Limah, Oman, on 3 Nov. Iran links reopening the strait to US concessions.
for_you: Follow UKMTO and flag-state guidance if operating in the region. Shipping delays and higher insurance costs feed through to delivery times and prices.

sources.title: bne IntelliNews — IRGC says four more tankers hit mines in Hormuz
IranWire — IRGC claims four tankers destroyed by mines
Al Jazeera — UKMTO reports tanker hit off Oman; Iran says US reply unconvincing

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
